acceptedAnswer.text: Hormone optimization means evaluating your full hormonal picture — testosterone, estradiol, DHEA-S, cortisol, and thyroid function together — rather than testing one marker in isolation, then building a plan around what that evaluation actually shows.

mainEntity.name: Is hormone therapy for men the same as TRT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not exactly. TRT is one form of hormone therapy — testosterone replacement specifically. Hormone therapy for men is broader. Depending on what your evaluation shows, treatment may involve TRT, support for your body's natural testosterone production, or addressing metabolic and recovery factors first.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a hormone specialist and a testosterone clinic?

acceptedAnswer.text: A testosterone clinic is generally centered around one hormone and one treatment path. A hormone specialist evaluates your broader hormonal and metabolic picture — including thyroid, cortisol, estradiol, and more — before recommending treatment.

Andropause refers to the gradual decline in testosterone that can occur with age. Symptoms can overlap with other hormonal, metabolic, sleep, and stress-related changes, which is why evaluation matters before assuming testosterone is the cause.

mainEntity.name: Are the symptoms of andropause the same as low testosterone?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can overlap, but they're not automatically the same thing. Fatigue, lower motivation, reduced recovery, and changes in body composition can have several causes. Lab testing and clinical evaluation help determine what's actually contributing.

mainEntity.name: Will hormone therapy affect my fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, depending on the treatment. Testosterone therapy specifically can affect sperm production and natural hormone signaling. That's why fertility goals should be discussed before treatment begins — especially if you're younger or considering having children in the future.

mainEntity.name: Do I need TRT, or could something else explain how I feel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly. TRT is one potential outcome of a full evaluation, not the default. If your results point toward thyroid, metabolic, sleep, stress, or recovery-related factors instead — or alongside testosterone — those may need to be addressed as part of your plan.

mainEntity.name: What does a hormone evaluation actually check?

acceptedAnswer.text: A comprehensive evaluation can include total and free testosterone, estradiol, SHBG, DHEA-S, cortisol, and thyroid markers, alongside the broader metabolic and physiologic picture. Looking at these together provides more context than a single testosterone result.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a referral to see a hormone specialist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Generally, no. You can schedule an evaluation directly. If you're already seeing another specialist for a related condition, RHM can work alongside that care rather than replacing it.
